purpose: A separate bounded exploratory CPU/memory adaptation comparison after RAM range calibration. Retain all outcomes; no topological inference or detector-superiority claim.

controller.decision: For cpu, ram and joint, take the next fixed transfer only if the preceding measured checkout outcome is safe, the measurement is valid, and advertising CPU throttling is positive. This is an output-pressure-motivated exploratory resource-transfer heuristic, not an optimizer or evidence of recipient memory pressure. Keep all realized gains and losses.
controller.control: Perform all six sham updates unless measurement infrastructure fails. A readable unsafe control outcome does not stop the history.
controller.stop: Stop adaptive histories after their first valid unsafe checkout epoch, absent/unobserved advertising CPU pressure, measurement failure or six moves.
controller.update_order: Update checkout, payment, shipping, then ad. Attempt every command even after a client error; archive every attempt and determine manipulation validity from persisted/live resource snapshots. CPU and memory are updated together per container, with swap disabled. Intermediate updates are not atomic.

analysis.witness: At the same measured epoch within a fresh-runner block, all four histories have valid initially safe baselines and valid measurements; control, cpu and ram are safe while joint is unsafe. Report every matched epoch, including alternative patterns. Do not impute later epochs after a policy stops.
analysis.frequency: Count blocks with at least one observed witness and show the number of fully valid blocks, observed complete four-way epochs, and missing or invalid data. This is a descriptive bounded-path observation, not a fixed-time causal estimand or a detector reliability estimate.
analysis.reward: Successful advertising responses per second, including zero output and all negative/zero changes. Allocation to advertising is not itself evidence of efficiency improvement. Inspect memory-only and joint reward effects separately.
analysis.failure_rule: Safe/unsafe depends exclusively on externally measured checkout p95 and unsuccessful scheduled iterations. Post-adaptation restart/OOM is diagnostic only, never an automatic exclusion or label override. Lost primary observations and resource-configuration mismatches are technical-invalid; retain every readable outcome.
analysis.scope: CPU and memory are separate compositions with their own fixed configured totals; workload intensity is fixed. The experiment does not establish downward closure of safe adaptations, a simplicial complex, or superiority over multivariate rules.
analysis.replacement_rule: Exactly 20 fresh-runner blocks, with no outcome-based replacements, extensions, additional waves, grid search or automatic parameter changes. Preserve all short, invalid and missing histories.
analysis.calibration_boundary: Instrumentation and the RAM range were exercised in a separate nine-condition engineering execution. It is not pooled with this campaign. Each new history must independently pass its baseline and effective-limit checks. No required witness or outcome fraction gates execution.

prior_engineering.observation: The earlier path ended at 64 MiB without observed memory-cap binding; its campaign did not start.

ram_calibration.observation: At fixed 0.30 checkout CPU, 48/40/36 MiB were safe without cap events; 32/28 MiB were safe with cap events; 24/20 MiB were unsafe with failed requests and OOM diagnostics. One observation per condition, not a certified threshold.

selection_provenance.rationale: Begin at the measured 48-MiB headroom point and transfer 4 MiB per move. Six moves traverse 32, 28 and 24 MiB. CPU transfers of 0.03 per move end at 0.12, the first unsafe checkout CPU in the earlier CPU-only engineering history; 0.14 had remained safe there. These are engineering-informed choices fixed before this new campaign, not a pilot-eligible selection, a tuned detector or a guarantee of a joint-only contrast.
